entries.note: A container leaving a terminal or depot. Its place among the moves decides: before any gate-in it is the empty container released to the shipper, the first truck gate-out after the last discharge is out for delivery, any other is transit.

A container entering a terminal or depot. Its place among the moves decides: the first before loading is the cargo accepted, the one after the gate-out for delivery is the empty container's return and the delivery, any other is transit.
Loaded on a vessel, a barge or a train.
Discharged at a port of transshipment or discharge.
A train's, barge's or truck's departure.
A train's, barge's or truck's arrival.
The cargo packed into the container, usually at the shipper's or a warehouse before the gate-in.
The cargo unpacked from the container, which may be a stop before delivery or the delivery itself.
The container collected at a customer's site, the shipper's or the consignee's; the wording does not say whose.
The container left at a customer's site, the shipper's or the consignee's; the wording does not say whose.
An inspection of the container, which does not move it on.
A new seal on the container, usually after an inspection.
The wording does not say what was removed or from where.
